colorRgbw.the_strip_has_a_separate_white: The strip has a separate white LED (W): it gives a cleaner white than mixing red + green + blue.

common.lead: The status light and the strip: states, colors, effects and outputs.

lights.this_machine_has_no_led_strip: This machine has no LED strip: there is nothing to send to the board.
lights.the_file_does_not_look_like: The file does not look like a lighting profile.
lights.the_file_is_not_a_valid: The file is not a valid lighting profile.
lights.profile_loaded_review_the_changes_and: Profile loaded: review the changes and save to apply them.
lights.couldn_t_read_the_configuration_is: Couldn't read the configuration (is the WorkshopService service running?)
lights.check_the_led_counts_and_that: Check the LED counts and that each strip has a different E number
lights.output_3_a_copy_of_the: Output 3: a copy of the Duet board LEDs (CAN, VIN, 12 V, 5 V, 3.3 V)
lights.output_2_the_indicator_of_this: Output 2: the indicator of this page, the sidebar, the DWC chip and the jog (always available)
lights.output_2_the_indicator_of_this_no_bar: Output 2: the indicator of this page, the DWC chip and the jog (always available)
lights.output_2_the_indicator_of_this_no_jog: Output 2: the indicator of this page, the sidebar and the DWC chip (always available)
lights.output_2_the_indicator_of_this_no_bar_no: Output 2: the indicator of this page and the DWC chip (always available)
lights.output_1_the_led_strip_connected: Output 1: the LED strip connected to the board
lights.here_you_decide_how_what_the: Here you decide how what the machine is doing is shown: on an LED strip (if you have one), on an indicator on the screens, and on a copy of the board LEDs. Every state says on which of the three outputs it is shown.

stateBadge.more_than_one_state_is_active: More than one state is active at the same time

stripZones.out_duet_help: The strip is connected to the board (M950). Every paint is a set of orders to the board.
stripZones.out_pi_help: The Pi sends the colours by itself through the SPI data pin (MOSI) and nothing goes to the board for this strip: every effect is complete and the board gets fewer calls. The strip is not used from the Duet any more.
stripZones.out_now_pi: Current output: pin GPIO{pin} of the Pi
stripZones.the_state_is_painted_on_the: The state is painted on the Status zone of the main strip.
stripZones.the_state_is_painted_on_that: The state is painted on that zone and the screens copy it. The Status zone of the main strip stays off.
stripZones.no_led_shows_the_state_the: No LED shows the state: the Status zone of the main strip stays off and the state is only seen on the screens.
stripZones.if_you_do_not_want_work: If you do not want work light on the strip, set 0 lighting LEDs in the Outputs tab.
stripZones.add_a_zone_with_its_color: Add a zone (with its color and its switch); then move it with the arrows
stripZones.status_zone_its_color_comes_from: Status zone: its color comes from the machine status
stripZones.move_toward_the_end_of_the: Move toward the end of the strip
stripZones.duet_np_led_connector_led_0: Duet NP_LED connector: LED 0 starts here
stripZones.move_each_zone_with_the_arrows: Move each zone with the arrows until it matches how your strip is connected. Every extra zone has its own color and switch.
stripZones.zones_in_strip_order_from_the: Zones in strip order, from the Duet connector
stripZones.is_not_in_config_g_add: is not in config.g: add a line like
stripZones.add_another_led_strip_another_duet: Add another LED strip (another Duet output)
stripZones.paints_each_zone_in_its_color: Paints each zone in its color for 6 s, with what you see here (even if not saved):
stripZones.lights_the_first_leds_for_6: Lights the first LEDs for 6 s. If the last LED of the strip stays off, raise the number; if nothing changes, lower it.
stripZones.how_many_leds_does_it_have: How many LEDs does it have?
stripZones.only_while_the_machine_isn_t: Only while the machine isn't working.
stripZones.the_board_takes_it_when_it: The board takes it when it restarts.
stripZones.a_copy_of_config_g_is: A copy of config.g is saved. Then the board must be restarted.
stripZones.the_strip_is_not_in_config: The strip is not in config.g: add a line like
stripZones.leds_all_are_shown_shrunk_to: LEDs: all are shown, shrunk to fit.
stripZones.number_in_m950_e_n_change: Number in M950 E<n>; change it only if the strip is on another output.
stripZones.the_ones_that_show_the_mode: The ones that show the mode and what the machine is doing.
stripZones.the_ones_that_give_work_light: The ones that give work light (from LED 0). Use 0 if you do not want light on the strip.

tabAdvanced.leave_it_off_to_move_a: Leave it off to move a profile to another machine without touching its strip.
tabAdvanced.also_include_the_strip_led_counts: Also include the strip (LED counts, zones, output)
tabAdvanced.export_saves_all_the_colors_states: Export saves all the colors, states, effects, scenes and schedules in a file. Import loads it into this page WITHOUT saving: review it and tap "Save and apply".
tabAdvanced.if_you_stop_or_disable_workshop: If you stop or disable "Lights and Status" in Settings > Plugins, the service switches the status zone of the strip off and stops painting and answering light commands. When you enable it again everything resumes by itself.
tabAdvanced.without_a_strip_there_is_nothing: Without a strip there is nothing to take back: if the service stops, the screens simply stop updating.
tabAdvanced.the_service_tells_the_board_every: The service tells the board every 2 s that it is painting the strip. If it stops telling for more than 10 s (it stopped or hung), the board takes the status LEDs back with the mode colors saved here, so they never freeze.
tabAdvanced.what_cannot_be_read_from_the: What cannot be read from the board: 5 V and 3.3 V have no measurement (they look on if the board answers). The BLTouch pin comes from global.probePinOut (macros deployprobe.g and retractprobe.g) or, if it does not exist, from M401.
tabAdvanced.the_service_could_not_read_the: The service could not read the board state: the dots look off.
tabAdvanced.no_data_yet_save_and_wait: No data yet: save and wait a few seconds (the WorkshopService service builds it).
tabAdvanced.tap_a_dot_or_hover_over: Tap a dot or hover over it to see what it is.
tabAdvanced.a_panel_that_only_exists_on: A panel that only exists on the screens and is never sent to any LED: one dot for everything the board reports (board LEDs, endstops, probes and the BLTouch pin, fans, heaters, laser or spindle and outputs).
tabAdvanced.a_strip_is_painted_in_order: A strip is painted in order from the board connector. Here you move the zones until they match your strip, add zones with their own color, choose which zone shows the state and add other LED strips.
tabAdvanced.things_that_almost_never_need_touching: Things that almost never need touching: the order of the zones on the strip, a board signals panel, how the system behaves if something fails, and saving or moving your whole lighting profile to another machine.
tabAdvanced.pi_section_what: By default the strip hangs from the Duet board and every repaint is a set of commands to the board. Here you can make the Pi send the colours by itself, through a data pin of the Pi, without calling the board. It is off and changes nothing until you turn it on, and it applies when you save.
tabAdvanced.pi_read_error: The pins of the Pi could not be read.
tabAdvanced.pi_row_switch: Use a pin of the Pi (instead of the Duet board)
tabAdvanced.pi_none_why: No pin of this Pi can drive a strip right now. A strip needs the data pin (MOSI) of an SPI bus that is on and free: the pins above are used by something else or their SPI bus is off.
tabAdvanced.pi_empty_why: This Pi offers no pin that can be chosen for a strip.
tabAdvanced.pi_enable_how: To enable a free SPI bus, add a line such as dtoverlay=spi1-1cs (SPI bus 1) to /boot/firmware/config.txt and restart the Pi. It is a system change that you make: this page does not do it. Then come back here.
tabAdvanced.pi_pins_loading: Reading the pins of the Pi...
tabAdvanced.pi_pin_no_strip: free, but a strip does not work here (it needs the MOSI pin of an SPI bus that is on)
tabAdvanced.pi_save_first: Save the changes to be able to test.
tabAdvanced.pi_wiring: Wiring: the strip needs its own 5 V supply, a common ground with the Pi and a 3.3 V to 5 V level shifter on the data line. This option has not been tested with a real strip.

tabColors.okabe_and_ito_palette_distinguishable_wi: Okabe and Ito palette (distinguishable with the most common forms of color blindness) and a different blink pattern on the main states.
tabColors.every_state_stop_pause_laser_firing: Every state (stop, pause, laser firing...) has its color and its effect in the States tab.
tabColors.how_strong_the_mode_color_looks: How strong the mode color looks when there is no job (strip only).
tabColors.seen_when_idle_and_as_a: Seen when idle and as a progress bar during a job.
tabColors.hands_out_different_effects_slow_blink: Hands out different effects (slow blink, double flash, pulse...) among the active states, to tell them apart without depending on color.
tabColors.they_change_the_colors_of_the: They change the colors of the modes and of the main states and the idle brightness; then you can adjust them one by one.
tabColors.the_color_of_each_mode_and: The color of each mode and the ready-made styles. The colors of each state are chosen in the States tab.

tabEffects.the_same_goes_for_a_crash: The same goes for a crash and for active risk: if the lighting has the status zone, they still warn.
tabEffects.show_the_no_limits_jog_even: Show the no-limits jog even when the status lights are off
tabEffects.the_blinking_while_paused_and_the: The blinking while paused and the other effects of each state are changed in the States tab (Effect column).
tabEffects.a_live_job_arrives_line_by: A live job arrives line by line: its end is detected when it is closed.
tabEffects.test_the_warning_on_the_strip: Test the warning on the strip
tabEffects.the_status_zone_blinks_for_a: The status zone blinks for a few seconds when a file job or a live job ends, so you notice even if you are not looking at the screen.
tabEffects.when_the_board_starts_an_animation: When the board starts, an animation fills the strip once and then each zone takes its color. "Show now" plays it with what you have on screen, without saving.
tabEffects.without_an_led_strip_there_are: Without an LED strip there are no animations to show: this tab is about the strip. The state is seen on the on-screen indicator.
tabEffects.the_strip_animations_and_effects_the: The strip animations and effects. The effect of each state (blink, pulse...) is chosen in the States tab.

tabLighting.with_every_led_at_maximum_you: With every LED at maximum you would exceed your supply limit. If you use very bright colors on the whole strip, lower the brightness or use a bigger supply.
tabLighting.current_the_strip_supply_can_give: Current the strip supply can give. 0 = do not warn.
tabLighting.every_rgbw_led_has_4_colors: Every RGBW LED has 4 colors (red, green, blue, white). 20 mA is typical.
tabLighting.an_estimate_to_know_whether_your: An estimate to know whether your supply copes: every color of every LED draws about 20 mA at full brightness. If you set your supply limit, the page warns when it is exceeded.
tabLighting.dim_the_strip_during_this_schedule: Dim the strip during this schedule
tabLighting.during_that_schedule_the_brightness_of: During that schedule the brightness of the whole strip goes down (so it does not dazzle or bother at night).
tabLighting.the_light_the_camera_turns_on: The light the camera turns on to take a photo keeps working the same: this auto-off never cuts it in the middle of a photo.
tabLighting.with_a_file_job_or_a: With a file job or a live job; if the light was already on it does nothing.
tabLighting.turn_the_light_on_when_a: Turn the light on when a job starts
tabLighting.counts_from_when_it_was_turned: Counts from when it was turned on or from the last machine activity.
tabLighting.turn_the_light_off_by_itself: Turn the light off by itself if nothing happens
tabLighting.so_the_light_is_not_left: So the light is not left on by mistake, and is ready when a job starts. The light the camera turns on for a photo is not touched.
tabLighting.so_the_light_is_not_left_no_camera: So the light is not left on by mistake, and is ready when a job starts.
tabLighting.changes_to_the_names_and_colors: Changes to the names and colors of the scenes are saved with "Save and apply".
tabLighting.turns_the_light_on_with_this: Turns the light on with this color and brightness
tabLighting.a_scene_is_a_named_color: A scene is a named color and brightness (work, photo, inspection...). One tap and the light stays like that, on. Up to 8.
tabLighting.the_strip_has_a_separate_white: The strip has a separate white LED: it gives a cleaner white light than mixing red, green and blue.
tabLighting.extra_zone_it_turns_on_at: Extra zone: it turns on at once.
tabLighting.when_off_the_lighting_also_uses: When off, the lighting also uses the status LEDs.
tabLighting.turns_the_lighting_on_or_off_2: Turns the lighting on or off now.
tabLighting.turns_the_lighting_on_or_off: Turns the lighting on or off and sets its color and brightness.
tabLighting.the_work_light_is_the_part: The work light is the part of the strip that lights the table. Everything about it is here; this tab only exists if the machine has an LED strip.
tabLighting.name: Name

tabOutputs.green_the_board_doesn_t_measure: Green. The board doesn't measure the 3.3 V: on if the board answers.
tabOutputs.red_the_board_doesn_t_measure: Red. The board doesn't measure the 5 V: on if the board answers.
tabOutputs.amber_on_if_the_board_measures: Amber. On if the board measures the internal 12 V (they come from the power supply).
tabOutputs.blue_on_with_the_board_supply: Blue. On with the board supply connected; off if it is missing (the board stays alive only on USB or external 5 V).
tabOutputs.red_blinks_slowly_when_the_board: Red. Blinks slowly when the board works and the expansion boards communicate over CAN; blinks fast if an expansion board does not synchronize or stopped answering; off if the board cannot be read.
tabOutputs.a_state_with_its_board_checkbox: A state with its "Board" checkbox ticked (States tab) covers these LEDs with its color while it lasts, for example so the emergency stop fills the whole zone.
tabOutputs.the_status_zone_has_few_leds: The status zone has few LEDs: at least one is always kept for the state, so only the first board LEDs you chose fit.
tabOutputs.the_board_leds_in_this_order: The board LEDs in this order: STATUS, VIN, 12 V, 5 V, 3.3 V. Hover to see each one.
tabOutputs.the_first_leds_are_the_status: The first LEDs are the status zone with the mode color; the last ones are the board ones in this order: STATUS, VIN, 12 V, 5 V, 3.3 V.
tabOutputs.preview_with_what_you_have_on: Preview (with what you have on screen, not saved)
tabOutputs.below_this_voltage_the_12_v: Below this voltage the 12 V LED looks off.
tabOutputs.below_this_voltage_the_vin_led: Below this voltage the VIN LED looks off (no supply).
tabOutputs.when_vin_and_12_v_go: When VIN and 12 V go off
tabOutputs.choose_at_least_one_board_led: Choose at least one board LED.
tabOutputs.it_copies_the_leds_the_duet_2: It copies the LEDs the Duet board has soldered on (CAN communication, VIN input, 12 V, 5 V and 3.3 V) with their colors and blinking. Without a strip they are only seen in the Summary tab.
tabOutputs.it_copies_the_leds_the_duet: It copies the LEDs the Duet board has soldered on (CAN communication, VIN input, 12 V, 5 V and 3.3 V) with their colors and blinking. They go at the end of the status zone: they do not add LEDs to the strip, they use the last ones of that zone.
tabOutputs.it_has_no_settings_of_its: It has no settings of its own: choose which states it shows with the "Screen" checkbox in the States tab.
tabOutputs.in_the_dwc_status_chip_available: In the DWC status chip, the small colored label of the Status panel in the Dashboard ("Available", "Processing"...): it takes the color of the state.
tabOutputs.at_the_top_of_the_controls: In the floating workshop sidebar (the one with the stop and shutdown buttons): below its header, and as a round dot when it is closed. Shown or hidden in the gear of that bar, option "Status lights at the top of the bar".
tabOutputs.at_the_top_of_this_page: At the top of this page, in the box with the name of the state.
tabOutputs.it_is_not_a_strip_it: It is not a strip: it is a badge with the name of the current state, its color and its effect, the reason and the list of active states. It is always available, with or without a strip, and shows what the service calculates.
tabOutputs.no_led_strip_everything_else_works: No LED strip. Everything else works the same: states, colors and effects are seen on the on-screen indicator. Save to apply it.
tabOutputs.turn_it_off_if_you_have: Turn it off if you have no strip: no light command is sent to the board and the lighting controls are hidden. The state is still seen on the screens.
tabOutputs.this_machine_has_an_led_strip: This machine has an LED strip
tabOutputs.a_physical_strip_neopixel_ws2812_sk6812: A physical strip (NeoPixel, WS2812 / SK6812), connected to the board or to a pin of the Pi (chosen below): one part gives work light and another shows the state.
tabOutputs.an_output_is_a_place_where: An output is a place where the machine state is shown. There are three and they are set up separately; in the States tab you choose which state goes to which.
tabOutputs.with_lighting: When the lighting takes the status zone
tabOutputs.with_lighting_help: The lighting uses the status zone when you turn the automatic status lights off. Choose what the board LEDs do at that moment.
tabOutputs.with_lighting_keep: They keep showing the board (as now)
tabOutputs.with_lighting_follow: They do the same as the zone: they light up or go off together with the lighting
tabOutputs.preview_status_zone_grey: The first dots (grey) are the status zone: its colour comes from the machine state. Then the board LEDs in this order: STATUS, VIN, 12 V, 5 V, 3.3 V.
tabOutputs.preview_follow_lighting: The automatic status lights are off and the board LEDs do the same as the zone: they show the lighting colour, like the status zone, and go off together with it.
tabOutputs.can_blink_fault: The CAN LED stays on and only blinks fast if there is a problem (recommended: less load)
tabOutputs.can_blink_always: The CAN LED blinks slowly like the one on the board (more load)

tabStates.the_last_shutdown_was_a_power: The last shutdown was a power cut or a hang. It turns off when you open the report in the Services page. Comes turned off.
tabStates.some_motor_is_released_m18_no: Some motor is released (M18): no power and no known position. Comes turned off.
tabStates.x_or_y_not_homed_with: X or Y not homed with the machine idle.
tabStates.a_live_job_is_open_but: A live job is open but the machine has gone a while without receiving moves (was it forgotten open?). Comes turned off.
tabStates.a_job_sent_live_line_by: A job sent live, line by line, through the G-code bridge.
tabStates.the_laser_power_is_greater_than: The laser power is greater than 0. Better with "Split the zone" (otherwise it covers the progress bar).
tabStates.homing_macro_or_tool_change_in: Homing, macro or tool change in progress.
tabStates.the_temperature_of_the_on_board: The temperature of the on-board computer went over the limit: check the fan. Comes turned off.
tabStates.an_rs485_device_with_no_axis: An RS485 device with no axis assigned has an alarm: it does not stop the machine, it only warns.
tabStates.an_rs485_servo_or_device_of: An RS485 servo or device of an axis has an alarm or does not answer.
tabStates.a_job_is_paused_or_pausing: A job is paused (or pausing / resuming).
tabStates.something_leaves_the_machine_without_a: Something leaves the machine without a protection: calibrating crash detection or PID, X/Y motors released. It is shown even if the automatic lights are off.
tabStates.the_jog_without_limits_mode_is: The jog "without limits" mode is active: it can move beyond the limits. It uses the color chosen in the jog.
tabStates.jog_color_help: The color of the jog without limits is chosen in the Jog (the same on the strip and the screens). It is only shown here.
tabStates.a_driver_detected_a_crash_15: A driver detected a crash (15 s) or a homed axis went out of its limits. It takes the whole zone.
tabStates.crash_or_axis_beyond_its_limits: Crash or axis beyond its limits
tabStates.the_motor_supply_is_off_m81: The motor supply is off (M81 or PSU Stop): no power to motors or laser even though the board is on.
tabStates.the_emergency_stop_was_pressed_and: The emergency stop was pressed and the board is halted. It is always shown and always wins.
tabStates.idle_color_and_progress_bar_during: idle color and progress bar during a job
tabStates.what_every_color_currently_seen_on: What every color currently seen on your outputs means (modes and enabled states).
tabStates.show_this_state_for_about_6: Show this state for about 6 s on the ticked outputs
tabStates.turn_this_state_on_or_off: Turn this state on or off
tabStates.fixed_state_always_above_the_others: Fixed state: always above the others
tabStates.this_machine_has_no_led_strip: This machine has no LED strip
tabStates.while_it_lasts_this_state_also: While it lasts, this state also covers the board LEDs at the end of the zone (they are turned on in the Outputs tab)
tabStates.show_this_state_on_the_on: Show this state on the on-screen indicator
tabStates.show_this_state_on_the_led: Show this state on the LED strip
tabStates.turn_on_the_ones_you_want: Turn on the ones you want to see. The arrows change the priority (the fixed ones do not move). "Test" shows it for about 6 seconds on the ticked outputs, with the color and effect you see here.
tabStates.the_emergency_stop_always_takes_the: The emergency stop always takes the whole zone, in any mode.
tabStates.example_with_two_enabled_states_and: Example with two enabled states and what you have on screen (not saved).
tabStates.see_the_example_on_the_strip: See the example on the strip (6 s)
tabStates.the_whole_zone_on_shared_among: The whole zone on, shared among the active states: the most important ones get more LEDs.
tabStates.the_active_states_take_turns_one: The active states take turns, one after another.
tabStates.the_whole_zone_shows_only_the: The whole zone shows only the highest-priority state.
tabStates.each_option_shows_the_real_state: Each option shows the REAL state of right now as it would look on the strip with that effect. Tapping it applies and saves it. The emergency stop, crash, risk and jog without limits always take the whole zone.
tabStates.each_option_shows_the_real_state_no_jog: Each option shows the REAL state of right now as it would look on the strip with that effect. Tapping it applies and saves it. The emergency stop, crash and risk always take the whole zone.
tabStates.when_several_are_active_at_once: When several are active at once
tabStates.the_automatic_status_lights_are_off: The automatic status lights are off: the lighting uses the status LEDs of the strip. What is on this tab is not seen on the strip until you turn them on (on the screens it is).
tabStates.change_one_of_each_pair_or: Change one of each pair, or give one a different effect, to tell them apart at a glance.
tabStates.colors_that_get_confused_modes_and: Colors that get confused (modes and enabled states with the same effect):
tabStates.every_row_is_something_the_machine: Every row is something the machine can be doing. It says when it turns on, what color it is, with which effect and on which of the three outputs (strip, screen, board) it appears. States at the top are more important than the ones below.
tabStates.zone_capacity: The status zone has {n} free LEDs (the board uses {b}): in Split mode {k} states fit at once.
tabStates.when_they_do_not_fit: When more states are active than LEDs
tabStates.fit_rotate: Show them in turns, one after another (none is lost)
tabStates.fit_hide: Show only the most important ones (the rest is visible on the screen)
tabStates.now_rotating: {n} states are active right now and only {k} fit: they are shown in turns.
tabStates.now_hidden: They do not all fit on the strip right now. Not shown on it: {names}. They are still visible on the screen.
tabStates.job_effects_help: Each blink or pulse is a command for the Duet. Without effects, the strip and the board LEDs stay in fixed colours while a job runs (file or live) and are repainted at most twice per second. Emergency stop, crash, risk, jog without limits, cancelling and paused keep their effect. The screens always animate.
tabStates.job_effects_help_no_jog: Each blink or pulse is a command for the Duet. Without effects, the strip and the board LEDs stay in fixed colours while a job runs (file or live) and are repainted at most twice per second. Emergency stop, crash, risk, cancelling and paused keep their effect. The screens always animate.
tabStates.job_effects_on: With the effects of each state, also during a job

tabSummary.there_are_no_changes_to_show: There are no changes to show yet.
tabSummary.up_to_50_changes_with_the: Up to 50 changes, with the time and how long each lasted. It is cleared when the service restarts.
tabSummary.with_every_led_at_maximum_you: With every LED at maximum you would exceed your supply limit. Not now, but beware of very bright colors.
tabSummary.what_is_lit_now_goes_over: What is lit now goes over your supply limit: lower the brightness or remove LEDs.
tabSummary.estimate_with_the_leds_lit_now: Estimate with the LEDs lit now and with all at maximum, to size the supply. It is not a measurement.
tabSummary.the_light_will_turn_itself_off: The light will turn itself off in about
tabSummary.turn_the_lighting_on_or_off: Turn the lighting on or off and pick a scene with one tap.
tabSummary.none_the_machine_only_shows_its: None: the machine only shows its mode.
tabSummary.everything_that_is_true_right_now: Everything that is true right now, from the most to the least important.
tabSummary.no_data_from_the_board_yet: No data from the board yet.
tabSummary.off_they_are_turned_on_in: Off: they are turned on in the Outputs tab.
tabSummary.status_can_vin_12_v_5: STATUS (CAN), VIN, 12 V, 5 V and 3.3 V as on the board. Hover to see each one.
tabSummary.at_the_top_of_this_page: At the top of this page and in the workshop sidebar.
tabSummary.at_the_top_of_this_page_no_bar: At the top of this page.
tabSummary.this_machine_has_no_led_strip: This machine has no LED strip. If you have one, turn it on in the Outputs tab.
tabSummary.live_copy_of_the_strip_connected: Live copy of the strip connected to the board.
tabSummary.live_copy_of_the_strip_on_the_pi: Live copy of the strip, which the Pi drives from one of its pins.
tabSummary.each_output_shows_the_state_its: Each output shows the state its own way; in the States tab you choose which state goes to which.
tabSummary.the_most_important_state_right_now: The most important state right now, with its color and effect. It is what the on-screen indicator shows.

startup.title: Start-up
startup.state_na: does not apply to your machine
startup.make_tip: Copies the example to the SD card. It never overwrites a file that already exists.
startup.edit_tip: Opens the file in the DWC editor.
startup.hide_tip: Hides this row on this screen. It does not delete anything.
startup.service_tip: It has to be running: it makes the examples and answers the buttons of this plugin.
startup.row_strip_tip: It is optional. If your machine has no strip, switch it off in the Outputs tab and this row turns grey.
startup.strip_none: no strip: nothing to set up
startup.row_m950: M950 line of the strip in config.g
startup.row_m950_tip: When the strip hangs from a Duet output, its M950 line (LED type, output and count) has to be in config.g. The Outputs tab creates or fixes it.
startup.row_pi_out_tip: A strip connected to the Pi needs a pin with SPI. It is chosen in the Outputs tab.
startup.pi_out_missing: the pin is still to be chosen (see Outputs)
startup.row_board_tip: A copy of the state on the board LEDs. It is optional.
startup.assist_tip: Walks you through what is missing, one thing at a time. You can skip what you do not need.
startup.assist_no_action: This cannot be fixed with a file from here. Read the explanation and, when you have it, tap "Check again".
startup.assist_done_ready: Everything you went through is ready.
startup.assist_done_left: {n} left to do. You can start again whenever you like.
startup.create_help_tip: Asks a few questions and builds the file. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
startup.questions_intro: Answer and I will build the file. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
startup.err_range: The number is outside the allowed range.
startup.err_chars: Do not use quotes, semicolons or line breaks.
startup.err_pattern: It does not have the expected format. See the help of this field.
startup.warn_moves: {n} line(s) that move the machine were commented out with ";". Check them and remove the ";" only when you are sure and the machine is free.
startup.warn_active: Lines without ";" really run when you use the button.
startup.plan_example: {file} only has the example (all commented). It is replaced by this one, and the previous text is kept in {backup}.
startup.plan_new: {file} already has your configuration and I will not overwrite it. This one will be saved apart as {target}; when you have checked it, rename it in Files > Macros.
startup.verify_ok: Done: the file exists, has active instructions and the plugin already sees it.
startup.verify_new: Saved as {file}. The plugin keeps using the previous file until you swap the names.
startup.verify_comments: {file} was saved, but all its lines are still commented, so the plugin still takes it as an example. That may be what you wanted.
startup.verify_notseen: {file} was saved, but the plugin does not see it as ready yet. Tap "Check again" in a few seconds.
startup.verify_missing: I could not read {file} back. Tap "Check again" to verify it.
startup.verify_fail: It could not be saved ({error}). Nothing was changed.
startup.plan_changed: The file changed while you were answering. Check again what is going to happen and confirm once more.
startup.modal_hint: Tap a card to set it up, or let it walk you through step by step.
startup.modal_sub: Get ready what this plugin needs from your machine
startup.row_strip_what: The LED strip of your machine, if you have one.
startup.row_strip_for: This plugin controls its colour, brightness and effects according to the state of the machine.
startup.row_strip_missing: Without a strip there is nothing to control. If you do not have one, turn it off in the Outputs tab and this row stops bothering you.
startup.row_m950_what: A line of your config.g (M950) that tells the Duet which type of LED you have, on which output and how many.
startup.row_m950_for: Without that line the Duet does not know the strip exists and cannot light it.
startup.row_m950_missing: The strip does not respond. The Outputs tab creates or fixes that line for you.
startup.row_pi_out_what: The pin of the Raspberry Pi where you connected the strip (it has to be an SPI pin).
startup.row_pi_out_for: The service talks to the strip through that pin.
startup.row_pi_out_missing: The strip connected to the Pi does not light. Choose the pin in the Outputs tab.
startup.row_board_what: The LEDs of the Duet board itself.
startup.row_board_for: They can copy the state of the machine, like the strip.
